svg.text: What's in Salander's backpack found by
Mikael?
Pipeline: v2.16 · Model: gpt-6-luna (high reasoning) ·
Latency: 21.3 s
Quality metrics: Retrieval context recall 100% · Generation
faithfulness 100% · Generation relevancy 100%
Mikael found a wallet with Salander’s ID, about 600 kronor,
200 U.S. dollars and a monthly travel card; cigarettes and
lighters; throat lozenges, tissues, a toothbrush, toothpaste,
tampons and condoms; a bound notebook, five pens, Mace,
makeup, an FM radio without batteries, and Saturday’s
Aftonbladet [E1]. There was also a hammer and a ring of six
keys, including apartment and padlock keys [E2].
CITED PASSAGES · 2
[E1] The Girl Who Played with Fire · Paragraph 19 ·
Page 56
When he had got home the morning after the attack on
Lundagatan, he opened the shoulder bag and spread the contents
on the kitchen table. There was a wallet with an ID card,
about 600 kronor, 200 American dollars, and a monthly travel
card. There was a pack of Marlboro Lights, three Bic lighters,
a box of throat lozenges, a packet of tissues, a toothbrush,
toothpaste, three tampons in a side pocket, an unopened pack
of condoms with a price sticker that showed they were bought
at Gatwick Airport in London, a bound notebook with stiff
black A4 dividers, five ballpoint pens, a can of Mace, a small
bag with makeup, an FM radio with an earphone but no
batteries, and Saturday’s Aftonbladet.
[E2] The Girl Who Played with Fire · Paragraph 22 ·
Page 56
The most intriguing item was a hammer, easily accessible in an
outside pocket. However, the attack had come so suddenly that
she had not been able to make use of it or the Mace. She had
evidently used her keys as brass knuckles—there were still
traces of blood and skin on them. Of the six keys on the ring,
three of them were typical apartment keys—front door,
apartment door, and the key to a padlock. But none of them fit
the door of the building on Lundagatan.
For what crime is Blomkvist tried and
convicted?
Pipeline: v2.16 · Model: qwen3.6:35b · Latency: 28.7 s
Blomkvist was tried and convicted of libelling and defaming
the financier Hans-Erik Wennerström. The court sentenced him
to three months in jail and 150,000 kronor in damages [E1].
CITED PASSAGES · 1
[E1] The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo · CHAPTER 1
Friday, December 20 · Paragraph 18 · Page 7
“Three months in gaol and 150,000 kronor damages. That’s
pretty severe,” said She from TV4. “I’ll survive.” “Are you
going to apologise to Wennerström? Shake his hand?” “I think
not.” “So you still would say that he’s a crook?” Dagens
Nyheter. The court had just ruled that Blomkvist had libelled
and defamed the financier Hans-Erik Wennerström. The trial was
over and he had no plans to appeal. So what would happen if he
repeated his claim on the courthouse steps? Blomkvist decided
that he did not want to find out.
